crime_highlights: Mr. Wheatley did board the bus to Vancouver, but became emotionally distressed as he neared the city
he instead went to the Downtown Eastside, where he remained for two days
When he was arrested, Mr. Wheatley had a crack pipe in his possession
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge erred in failing to particularly consider Mr. Wheatley's Aboriginal circumstances and the Gladue factors
The sentence she imposed was, in my view, unfit as a consequence of this failure
the judge was required to take into account Mr. Wheatley's circumstances as an Aboriginal offender
His background may, for example, make his anxiety over reporting to a residential facility more understandable

crime_highlights: The appellant forced his way into a restaurant in the early morning hours of July 18, 2016, and stole $2,200 in cash and an iPhone
in one of the theft under counts, the appellant stole almost $5,000 worth of jewelry from a business premises
the appellant broke the glass door of a public transit bus in the course of a dispute with the bus driver
the appellant's threat to break his landlord's cell phone
rationale_highlights: The appellant is a 33-year-old significantly disadvantaged Aboriginal offender
the judge noted the appellant's difficult upbringing and personal circumstances and his status as a disadvantaged Aboriginal offender
note: Court never states Aboriginal status reduced the sentence; appeal dismissed.

crime_highlights: Cindy Scow was beaten to death by the appellant Mr. Johnny in a dark, abandoned house
Ms. Scow, the 28-year-old mother of seven children, suffered extensive blunt-force injuries
she was struck at least six times to the head alone
He told some members of his family that he had beaten up Ms. Scow
Ms. Scow was pronounced dead at the Port Hardy Hospital in the early morning of September 10, 2012
rationale_highlights: because of alcohol and other systemic factors, the offender's degree of culpability is reduced
Mr. Johnny was 19 years old and intoxicated at the time of the offence
a sentence of 96 months is, in my opinion, unfit in this instance
the sentence must reflect his circumstances as an Aboriginal offender as required by s. 718.2(e) of the Code
note: Systemic reasoning partly via comparison with Pop.
